report:
## Conclusion: Your skepticism is well supported by the scientific evidence

The claim that abortion increases breast cancer risk is not supported by high-quality research and is rejected by every major scientific and medical body that has reviewed the evidence.

**The consensus view.** In 2003, the U.S. National Cancer Institute convened over 100 leading experts on pregnancy and breast cancer to review population-based, clinical, and animal studies. The panel concluded that induced abortion is not associated with an increase in breast cancer risk (cancer.gov, https://www.cancer.gov/types/breast/abortion-miscarriage-risk). The American Cancer Society similarly states that "higher-quality studies have generally found no link between abortions and breast cancer risk," noting that a 2018 National Academies of Sciences report reached the same conclusion (https://www.cancer.org/cancer/risk-prevention/medical-treatments/abortion-and-breast-cancer-risk.html).

**Why some studies suggested a link.** The claim largely stems from older case-control studies that relied on women's self-reported abortion history. Because cancer patients tend to be more forthcoming than healthy controls about a sensitive event like abortion (recall/reporting bias), these studies produced spurious associations. Large, prospective cohort studies avoid this flaw by using medical records rather than self-report. The landmark 1997 Danish study by Melbye et al., covering 1.5 million women via national registries, found no overall link—and it is far more methodologically reliable than the earlier case-control studies (New York Times, https://www.nytimes.com/1997/01/09/us/big-study-finds-no-link-in-abortion-and-cancer.html).

**Ongoing advocacy vs. science.** Journalistic investigation has traced continued promotion of the "abortion-breast cancer link" largely to advocacy organizations rather than mainstream oncology research, which has moved on from the hypothesis (The Atlantic, https://www.theatlantic.com/national/2013/12/inside-faulty-science-abortion-breast-cancer-link/355850/).

**Bottom line:** The best available evidence indicates no causal link between abortion and breast cancer risk.
